title: gpu-memory-slab-corruption-sleuthing-journal-2026-08
content:
Purpose:
This is a working investigation journal and initial runbook draft for a recurring class of GPU instability where long-running inference fleets intermittently see process kills, driver resets, and evidence of in-kernel GPU memory allocator corruption. Primary symptoms were observed on A100 nodes in our west-1 cluster with mixed NVLink peer traffic between tenant workloads.

Executive summary (short):
- Multiple jobs over 2026-08-07 -> 2026-08-10 were aborted with SIGKILL / driver reset.
- dmesg shows repeated references to slab/object corruption inside the NVIDIA kernel module (see samples below).
- Corruption correlates with heavy peer-to-peer NVLink traffic and sustained small-allocation churn from the runtime (many small KV cache allocations).
- Temporary mitigations (node cordon, driver restart, disabling peer access on suspect jobs) stop immediate failures but recurrence suggests a kernel/driver state leak under specific allocation patterns.

Why we care:
- Impacts Dedicated pools where multiple customers share NVLink fabric (we expose P2P in those SKUs), causing noisy-neighbor crashes and costly job restarts.
- Hard to reproduce in the lab; appears to need: high allocation churn + NVLink cross-device memcpy + CUDA context churn (many short-lived processes).

Timeline (important events):
- 2026-08-07 02:41 UTC: First alert, node gpu-west-1a-32 returned multiple ContainerOOMKilled events.
- 2026-08-07 02:45 UTC: Oncall bootstrapped node, collected dmesg and nvidia-smi -q snapshots; applied cordon and restarted kubelet.
- 2026-08-07 03:05 UTC: Observed driver reset on node during post-reboot job reschedule.
- 2026-08-08 16:22 UTC: Repeat failure on different node with similar dmesg signatures. Attach logs to JIRA-INFR-7891.
- 2026-08-10 09:30 UTC: Run experimental repro in isolated lab instance (see experiment notes).

Observed logs (representative snippets):
- dmesg: "nvidia: kernel slab corruption: object 0xffff8880a7b3c000 links corrupted at offset 0x40"
- dmesg: "nvidia: nvlink_peer_copy: failed dma_map error -12"
- journalctl (nvidia-driver): "watchdog: GPU 0 hung for 30000ms, resetting client contexts"
- container stderr: "cudaErrorIllegalAddress: device kernel trap detected"

Checks we ran (commands used):
- nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION > /tmp/gpu_snapshot_$(hostname)_$(date +%s).txt
- sudo dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg_tail.txt
- sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver.service --since "2026-08-07" > /tmp/driver_journal.txt
- kubectl describe pod <id> to capture OOM/oom_kill info and cgroup usage
- cuda-memcheck --tool leakcheck ./simple-p2p-copy-test (lab repro)

Repro experiment (lab):
Setup:
- 2x A100 PCIe, NVLink enabled, same kernel/driver as prod (520.61.05) on a stripped down Fedora VM.
- Containerized workload that does many small cudaMalloc/cudaFree cycles while concurrently launching cross-device cudaMemcpyAsync over NVLink (4k-64k sizes)
- Stress driver with high concurrency (8 worker threads per process)

Result:
- After ~25 minutes, one worker hit cudaErrorIllegalAddress, dmesg matched slab corruption signature.
- Enabling CUDA LAUNCH_BLOCKING made repro slightly faster (indicates timing-sensitive).
- Disabling peer access (cudaDeviceDisablePeerAccess) prevented repro in lab for runs up to 2 hours.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) NVLink DMA engine + driver slab allocator race: small/fragmented allocations lead to stale pointers being reused while DMA still referenced them (timing race). Explains why disabling P2P removes repro.
2) Driver bug triggered by ECC-correction bursts: when ECC correctable errors spike, the driver attempts internal scrubs and may cause allocation ordering changes that expose a latent slab bug. (We saw small CCE spikes in some cases.)
3) Hardware memory cell deterioration on specific cards: less likely because failures occur across multiple cabinets and respond to driver restart.

Immediate mitigation (runbook - emergency steps):
1) Detect and isolate: when we see "kernel slab corruption" lines in dmesg, cordon the node immediately: kubectl cordon <node>.
2) Evacuate non-critical jobs: drain with --ignore-daemonsets and --delete-local-data to avoid hung pods: kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force.
3) Restart NVIDIA persistence daemon and driver: sudo systemctl restart nvidia-persistenced && sudo modprobe -r nvidia && sudo modprobe nvidia (note: modprobe -r may fail if processes hold gpu contexts; prefer node reboot if driver reload unsuccessful).
4) For affected tenants, offer fallback to Dedicated nodes with NVLink disabled or to non-P2P SKUs. Ops playbook: reach out via support template in JIRA-INFR-7891.
5) If a quick driver downgrade/upgrade is feasible (per patch guidance), schedule a rolling update for nodes matching the failure fingerprint.

Runbook - onboarding steps for oncall (short checklist):
- Step 0: Triage console: check node metrics for ECC correctable bursts, GPU utilization spikes, cuda context churn.
- Step 1: pull dmesg + journalctl + nvidia-smi snapshots and attach to JIRA ticket.
- Step 2: attempt graceful drain; if pods stuck in Terminating > 5m, escalate to SRE senior.
- Step 3: attempt driver restart. If modprobe -r fails or driver reload requires reboot, schedule immediate reboot during low-traffic window.

Longer-term remediation candidates (owners assigned):
- Kernel/driver upgrade evaluation: try driver family 525.x (owner: Marcelo Ruiz) — confirm whether upstream contains slab fixes for allocator. (linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1245)
- NVLink isolation policy: add k8s node label for "nvlink-enabled" and restrict P2P workloads to labeled nodes with stricter tenancy (owner: Lena Zhou).
- Add an accelerator-side watchdog metric: emit counts for "gpu_driver_slab_corruption_detected" and alert after N events in T window (owner: Aisha Patel).
- Improve CI repro harness: add synthetic p2p allocation churn test to nightly GPU regression suite (owner: Tom Whitaker).
- Work with vendor field rep to run memtest-like endurance on suspect cards (owner: Ethan Ramirez).

Metrics and alerting (proposal):
- Alert name: GPU_Driver_Slab_Corruption_Detected. Trigger when dmesg contains pattern "kernel slab corruption" OR driver journal contains "memory corruption" more than 1x in 15m across a single node.
- Secondary alert: Elevated ECC_CE_Rate combined with driver-reset rate > 1/hr.

Open action items (short):
- [ ] Attach full dmesg/driver logs to JIRA-INFR-7891 (Ethan) - in progress
- [ ] Run extended lab repro with different driver versions (Marcelo) - queued
- [ ] Implement node label + scheduler constraint for NVLink (Lena) - planning
- [ ] Add alert rule and Grafana panel for slab-corruption pattern (Aisha) - TODO
- [ ] Add p2p-stress to nightly (Tom) - TODO

Notes / miscellany (freeform):
- We saw one case where disabling ECC interrupts at the firmware layer temporarily reduced the frequency of occurrences; this aligns with hypothesis #2 but is not an acceptable prod mitigation for customers relying on ECC. Logging that observation for vendor follow-up.
- There are historical Slack threads referencing similar signatures in 2025-10 but with different driver version; worth cross-referencing before proposing a blanket driver upgrade.
- Be cautious about rolling driver changes without staged canaries — driver reloads can trigger service-impacting reboots if not coordinated.

Appendix: useful commands and quick paste-ins
- Collect snapshot: mkdir -p /var/tmp/gpu-debug && sudo dmesg --ctime > /var/tmp/gpu-debug/dmesg.txt && nvidia-smi -q -d MEMORY,UTILIZATION > /var/tmp/gpu-debug/nvidia_snapshot.txt && sudo journalctl -u nvidia-driver.service -n 1000 > /var/tmp/gpu-debug/driver_journal.txt
- Quick check for pattern: sudo dmesg | grep -i "slab corruption" || sudo journalctl -k | grep -i nvidia | tail -n 200
- Lab repro command (container): docker run --rm --gpus all redwood/gpu-p2p-stress:latest /stress --alloc-churn --p2p-copy --workers 8 --size-min 4096 --size-max 65536 --duration 3600

If you are reading this while oncall: add any new findings below with timestamps. If you make a change to prod (cordon, reboot, driver update) please add a short note describing the outcome so we can quickly iterate the runbook.

Journal entries: (edit as you go)
- 2026-08-10 10:05 Ethan: reproduced in lab with 520.61.05; disabling P2P prevented repro. Attached driver logs to ticket.
- 2026-08-11 14:40 Marcelo: ran driver 525.85 test; initial run (90m) did not reproduce, scheduling longer run.
- 2026-08-12 08:12 Lena: started k8s node labeling experiment in staging pool; no customer-facing traffic yet.

End of doc.
